rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are the leaders who mislead people and whose attitude is under discussion in the sūrah.
rows.anchor: It refers to the leaders who led people astray and whose attitude is under discussion in this sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those leaders have vested interests in wrongdoing, so they resist a messenger's reform and try by any means to curb his call to truth.
rows.anchor: since they have vested interests in all these evils, they do not easily tolerate his invitation towards the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet can be assured that his Lord suffices to help and guide him through hardship.
rows.anchor: his Lord is sufficient to help and guide him in every hardship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ascribes the respite given to evil to Himself as part of His established practice, discussed at length in al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: He has ascribed it to Himself. This established practice of God is referred to at many instances in this exegesis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi identifies a fourth objection: opponents said a divine Qur’an should have been revealed all at once, reinforcing their claim that others coauthored it.
rows.anchor: This verse cites their fourth objection. They would spread this propaganda against the Qur’ ān in the hearts of people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could reveal the whole Book at once, but the Prophet could not receive and bear it all at once, and people could not learn from it effectively.
rows.anchor: it would not have been possible for the Prophet (sws) to receive it at once nor could the people have been taught effectively.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gradual lessons let the Prophet bear the Qur’an’s burden and gave willing learners an opportunity to learn.
rows.anchor: so that he could bear it and those who want to learn are provided with this opportunity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl means reading and reciting in a very thorough manner.
rows.anchor: means to read and recite in a very thorough way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tartīl expression is coordinated with a verb suppressed after kadhalika.
rows.anchor: the verb which is suppressed after

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The careful, piecemeal lessons show divine favor, making gradual revelation a reason for gratitude rather than objection.
rows.anchor: The implication is that the piecemeal revelation of the Qur’ ān should be a reason of expressing gratitude and not raising objections.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No divine scripture was revealed all at once: only the Ten Commandments came to Moses together on tablets, while the rest of the Torah was revealed during his life.
rows.anchor: Only the ten commandments were revealed in one instalment. They were given to Moses (sws) written on tablets.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gospel consists of Jesus’s wise sermons revealed on different occasions as needs arose, and the Psalms of David’s hymns and counsels were likewise revealed on separate occasions.
rows.anchor: the Gospel is composed of the sagacious sermons of Jesus (sws) which were revealed to him at various instances according to the needs that arose.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets were preachers, teachers, and moral mentors charged with reforming an ailing nation, so they received guidance gradually as needed.
rows.anchor: They were preachers, teachers and moral mentors. They had to cure an ailing nation and purify their beliefs and deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No People of the Book scholar, as far as Islahi knows, claims that their scriptures were revealed at once; such a claim would contradict those books.
rows.anchor: none of the scholars of the People of the Book has ever claimed if any of their books was revealed at once.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the exegetes’ opinion that the Torah, Psalms, and Gospel were each revealed all at once.
rows.anchor: The opinion of our exegetes who say that the Torah, Psalms and the Gospel were revealed in one go is thus not correct too.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term rendered as an example also means objection here; its parallel with al-ḥaqq indicates that the objection is baseless.
rows.anchor: used in parallel to it, the implication is that the objection referred to is baseless.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After answering the objections, God reassures the Prophet: his mission was commanded by God, his nation had turned against him, and God would defend him.
rows.anchor: The need for this assurance was because it was at God’s behest that he preached about his prophethood and invited people to the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā after yuḥsharūna makes the verb carry the sense of being dragged, as in 54:48.
rows.anchor: shows that the latter verb encompasses the meaning

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse contrasts with 25:24: the people of Paradise receive good news, while the people of Hell face their fate.
rows.anchor: This whole verse occurs in contrast with verse 24. The dwellers of Paradise are given glad tidings of a goodly fate in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about being most astray points to people who cannot see where their worldly path leads; in the Hereafter they will recognize its destination and course.
rows.anchor: When the destination of Hell will come before them in the hereafter, then they will realize the beginning and end of their journey!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Moses and Noah narratives and intervening peoples assure the Prophet and warn his nation: earlier communities mocked messengers who taught them and ultimately suffered a terrible fate; the next sūrah gives these events in detail.
rows.anchor: The purpose is to assure the Prophet (sws) and warn his nation that God sent His teachings to these nations as well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence is ascending for Moses, the prominent Israelite prophet given a Book and law, then Noah, from whom prophets came after Abraham; intervening nations are named in descending order.
rows.anchor: Their sequence of mention is both ascending and descending. First, Moses (sws) is mentioned who was the most prominent prophet and messenger of the Israelites

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron’s repeated mention as Moses’s helper highlights God’s favor and His conclusive communication of truth through a messenger assisting another.
rows.anchor: The purpose is to explain an aspect of God’s favour and His conclusive communication of the truth: a messenger was sent to assist another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses considered himself inexpressive and prayed for Aaron’s eloquence and persuasive power to help him preach effectively; God granted the prayer and sent both to Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: Thus he prayed to God to make Aaron his helper so that through his eloquence and power of persuasion he would be able to preach his message with full force and confidence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his people failed to value this divine favor and blessing.
rows.anchor: However, they did not value this favour and blessing of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s people denied the messengers’ signs as magic and were utterly routed; this assures the Prophet that perverted hearts reject guidance and warns Quraysh of the same consequence.
rows.anchor: the Almighty sent both these messengers with His signs to these people but they rejected them by regarding them to be magic.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s people rejected one messenger, yet the plural messengers is used because they all brought the same message from the same Sender, so rejecting one means rejecting all.
rows.anchor: since all the messengers present the same message and since the one who sent them is also the same, the rejection of one is tantamount to the rejection of all.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This plural usage makes people consider where denying a single messenger leads them.
rows.anchor: This style is meant to direct the attention of people to the fact that those who deny a messenger should contemplate where this denial actually takes them to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being made an exemplary sign points to the horrible fate of people who reject their messenger.
rows.anchor: The words “and made them an exemplary sign for people” point to the horrible fate of people who deny their messenger.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment extends beyond this world to painful torment in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: God does not merely punish such wrongdoers in this world; in the hereafter too, He punishes them in a very painful way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for destroying is omitted because contextual indications make it understood.
rows.anchor: is suppressed due to concomitant indications.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says he has not been able to identify the Companions of al-Rass with certainty.
rows.anchor: I regret that I have not been successful until now about the identity of

rows.speaker: Ibn Jarīr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr offers several possible identities for al-Rass’s people, but he endorses none and says no identification can be stated with certainty.
rows.anchor: Ibn Jarīr33 has cited several names but he himself is not satisfied about either of them.
